title: Power Apps: build model-driven apps with Copilot Cowork
summary: Hold: the spending-policy navigation stops at opening the wizard, before the choices that grant Cowork access and configure credit limits. The roadmap facts and licensing are supported. The Graph call exists, but its note should identify the request properties that select Cowork and set limits.

claims.claim: Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy is the complete path to the Cowork access and credit-limit control.
claims.quote: Create and name the policy and then choose Identity as the scope. ... switch to Specific groups and select the directory group. ... Select the agents and services that users and groups in this policy can access.
claims.fix: The printed path only opens the wizard. Set controls[0].ui.docs to https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/usage-based-billing-manage-copilot-credits and extend the front-matter and rendered path to 'Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy > Identity > Specific groups > Select agents and services > Cowork > Set limits and alerts'. The cited governance page also explicitly requires choosing Specific groups and selecting Cowork after opening the wizard.

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies creates a spending policy with service selection and credit limits.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies ... Required properties are displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and serviceSettings. ... { "serviceId": "cowork", "state": "enabled" }
claims.fix: Keep the call. Add to controls[0].note and the rendered note: 'The request sets serviceSettings with serviceId cowork and state enabled, and sets periodLimit and perUserLimit. Group policies are created disabled; link their audience before the service enables them.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/cost-management/spendingpolicy-create, whose example and request-body reference document these properties and lifecycle.

claims.claim: Cowork spending policies can be scoped to security groups.
claims.quote: On the Scope user and group step, choose Specific groups and select the security group.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Users in scope of a spending policy that selects Cowork receive Cowork access.
claims.quote: Any user in the scope of a spending policy that selects Cowork can use Cowork, regardless of how small the credit limit is.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: A low credit limit does not prevent Cowork access.
claims.quote: A policy with a limit of one credit still grants access. To remove access for a user, remove them from every spending policy that includes Cowork. A low credit limit doesn't block access.

claims.claim: Removing a user from every spending policy selecting Cowork removes their access.
claims.quote: If no policy in scope selects Cowork, the user has no access.

claims.claim: The Cowork entry under Agents > All Agents no longer controls who can use Cowork.
claims.quote: The Cowork agent entry is still visible under Agents > All Agents, but any configuration on it has no effect on who can use Cowork.

claims.claim: Cowork credit-limit enforcement is asynchronous, so a user can sometimes start tasks after reaching a limit.
claims.quote: Credit consumption and limit enforcement are evaluated asynchronously, so a user might be able to start one or more tasks after their limit is reached before enforcement takes effect.
